label: rem:h2o-c2v-from-projector
title: $C_{2v}$ as the stabiliser of the H₂O assembly projector
html:
Interpretation of the H_2O molecular braid.

The two hydrogen sub-units of water carry equal strand counts. The exchange H_1 \leftrightarrow H_2 fixes the strand-partition \lambda = (24,2,2) and hence the assembly projector e_{\lambda,\mu}. That S_2 stabiliser is the C_{2v} point symmetry of the molecule — a C_2 rotation about the bisector of the H–O–H angle, fixing oxygen.

This instantiates the general principle that a structure's point symmetry is the stabiliser of its assembly projector. The same mechanism gives benzene's three equal acetylene units the ring symmetry S_3 (via e_{(2,2,2),(6)}). Water and benzene are the S_2 and S_3 instances of one categorical statement. The same reading, applied to the inter-molecular operator that forms a condensed phase, extends the principle from molecular point groups to the symmetries of phases of matter.
